harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Recovered both staged jobs into the working CUPS queue `archive`. J100 and J101 each have exactly one byte-identical archived payload, and their original spool files remain intact. CUPS and the queue persisted across node1’s reboot. Two raw probe jobs were also archived to verify current and post-reboot submissions.
actions_performed: Installed Ubuntu 7.10-compatible CUPS 1.3.2 without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created an idempotent electronic-archive backend targeting `/srv/legacy2/print-spool-recovery/printed`.
Configured and enabled the raw CUPS queue `archive`.
Processed J100 and J101 exactly once through CUPS.
Verified new raw submissions follow the same archive path.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified a changed boot identity, recovered service, preserved data, and a successful post-reboot job.

evidence.requirement: Working CUPS queue named archive using legacy-compatible software.
evidence.summary: CUPS 1.3.2-1ubuntu7.10 is running; `archive` is idle/enabled and targets the electronic archive backend.

evidence.requirement: Process every staged job exactly once while retaining bytes and original spool files.
evidence.summary: J100 and J101 each have one archived file, pass byte comparisons, and retain their original 28-byte and 31-byte spool files.

evidence.requirement: New raw jobs follow the same archive path.
evidence.summary: Pre- and post-reboot probe jobs completed through `archive`; each archived payload has the same hash as its submitted source.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel.

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 715a680f-85f9-4aa3-8af6-82b88738fe22 was captured; reboot was acknowledged; post-reboot ID changed to 0c650d40-19ee-4e54-94d5-5195af0ac377; CUPS, queue configuration, archived data, completed jobs, and new-job processing recovered.
